deployment_decisions.consistency: local single-writer file-backed state; use atomic replacement/checkpoint digests where implemented; no distributed replication guarantee
deployment_decisions.cap_pacelc: CAP is not applicable to the current single-process deployment. If shared across nodes, choose a transactional/consensus-backed store before enabling concurrent writers; consistency takes priority over availability for authoritative memory updates.

deployment_decisions.consistency: one authoritative supervisor writes a task checkpoint; digests and run/intent/plan identity reject stale state, but there is no distributed lease/fencing token yet
deployment_decisions.cap_pacelc: Do not run competing supervisors against the same state root. A distributed deployment must add leases plus monotonically increasing fencing generations; reject stale-owner commits even during partitions.

deployment_decisions.boundary: crew handoff queue and retry ledger
deployment_decisions.consistency: durable bounded local queue, idempotent handoff IDs, shared task retry budget, and persisted independent-review receipts; replay is at-least-once at the orchestration boundary
deployment_decisions.cap_pacelc: No transport-level exactly-once side effects are claimed. External tools must supply idempotency keys or compensation; multi-node queue publication requires a transactional outbox/inbox or equivalent.

deployment_decisions.consistency: digest-bound canonical JSON receipts tied to intent and source snapshot; promotion requires verified evidence and authorized decision records
deployment_decisions.cap_pacelc: Authoritative evidence/promotion state is consistency-first. During a partition, block promotion rather than accepting stale or conflicting receipts; replicas/quorum are not implemented in the local runtime.

deployment_decisions.consistency: provider/adapter-owned timeout, retries, and effect semantics; proposal adapters do not imply execution authority
deployment_decisions.cap_pacelc: PACELC latency/consistency trade-offs are provider-specific. AUREN does not promise exactly-once remote effects; use per-operation idempotency keys and explicit compensation for multi-step effects.
